headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and auto-execute interaction: Windsurf can read/write local workspace while the course agent writes files and handles secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads local files in a course workspace, while agent B shares state via the local filesystem and can ingest workspace files. That creates a plausible prompt-injection bridge through files, even though no direct shared channel is explicitly documented. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent A writes attacker-controlled text into a workspace file that agent B later opens
IF agent B treats workspace file contents as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic file ingestion for agent B
Review any file-based prompts before opening them
Use read-only mounts for agent A outputs where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-originated instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles configuration secrets and academic papers, and agent B has broad network egress plus local-filesystem sharing. If A’s workspace or secrets are visible to B, B can transmit them outward by default. Because the pair includes a local filesystem bridge and broad egress, the blast radius includes exfiltration and is dangerous in default use.
conditions: IF agent A stores secrets or sensitive papers in the shared workspace
IF agent B reads those files and sends context to remote services
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared workspace
Disable network egress for agent B during shared-workspace sessions
Use separate OS users or containers
Rotate any exposed keys immediately after a shared run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, and agent B also modifies git state while sharing state via the local filesystem. Agent A runs shell/subprocesses and writes files in a local development environment, so concurrent edits can collide and corrupt work or repository state. The overlap is explicit in both profiles, and the lack of locking makes the conflict materially risky.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same checkout or workspace
IF agent B auto-saves while agent A is writing files or running shell commands
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Disable auto-commit or auto-format on shared paths
Use git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing/RAG system that can produce outputs from papers and search flows, and agent B is a coding IDE agent that can act on workspace content. If B consumes A’s generated text without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or actions. This is not proven by direct integration, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF agent B uses agent A’s generated text as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step checks A’s outputs before B acts
mitigations: Require a review step before B acts on A outputs
Keep A outputs in a separate notes file
Add source citations to A-generated claims
Limit B to read-only analysis for A outputs
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic papers in a local development environment, while agent B is a closed-source editor agent with broad network egress and optional BYOK. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different handling and retention surfaces that can create policy gaps on the same data class. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential data is placed into the shared workspace
IF organizational policy requires stricter retention or residency controls than either profile documents
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace
Document retention expectations for both tools
Disable cloud sync for sensitive projects
Review vendor security docs before deployment
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-specific routing and retention
